sampling_model.design: Known fixed \(r=2\) Conflict Graph Design using the formal direct-effect conflict graph \(\mathcal H_n=I_n+A_{G_n}\), generated from independent desired-exposure coordinates in Perron-priority rank order.
sampling_model.units: One triangular array of \(n\) fixed labeled units with fixed graph and fixed potential outcomes; there is no super-population sampling.
sampling_model.treatment: The only randomness is \(U_{n,i}\), and Algorithm 1 maps it to the realized binary assignment \(Z_n\).
sampling_model.overlap: The endpoint exposure probability is known exactly as \(q_{n,i}=(4\lambda_n)^{-1}t_n^{|B_{n,i}|}\); for edgeless \(G_n\), \(\lambda_n=1\), \(B_{n,i}=\varnothing\), and \(q_{n,i}=1/4\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no statistical nuisance functions; \(\lambda_n\), \(q_{n,i}\), and \(\mathbf V_n\) are design-computable.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 5.6 proves asymptotic normality when the maximum conflict degree is \(o(n^{1/9})\).
Proposition 5.8 constructs a direct-effect sequence whose standardized CGD estimator does not converge in distribution.
Propositions 5.3 and 5.4 establish additive and ratio consistency, respectively, for the spectral variance-bound estimator.
Corollary 5.7 gives conservative Wald coverage under the paper's sufficient CLT regime.

Theorem 2.3 gives a Kolmogorov bound for dependency-graph sums with finite \(L^{\delta}\) moments for \(\delta\in[3,\infty)\); the direct fourth-moment substitution here sets \(\delta=4\). Theorem 2.1 is the bounded-summand result, and Theorem 2.4 treats \(\delta\in(2,3)\), so neither is the direct comparison for this class.
The discrete-time theorem bounds martingale normal approximation using increment moments and normalized predictable quadratic variation.
The paper characterizes admissible estimable conservative quadratic variance bounds under interference and complex designs.
The preprint derives design-based upper and lower bounds on minimax mean-squared point-estimation risk in terms of local and global conflict-graph connectivity.

body.tldr: For the fixed \(r=2\) component-Perron Conflict Graph Design estimator, the sharp worst-case uniform normal-inference frontier is \(d_n=o(n^{2/3})\), with no additional slowly varying boundary factor. The proved quantitative bound is \(C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)\{D_n^2/(n\lambda_n)+D_n/n\}^{1/5}\); repeated Perron-ordered stars give the legal non-Gaussian Gaussian--Poisson obstruction at the critical scale. The observable spectral variance-bound estimator is uniformly ratio-consistent in the normal regime and yields conservative feasible Wald coverage. In addition, the graph-adaptive condition \(D_n^2/(n\lambda_n)\to0\) is a sufficient pointwise rule for all three conclusions. Only the exact interior Kolmogorov rate, matched legal lower arrays for its vanishing terms, and optimized constants remain open.

project_justification.gap: The published CGD theorem proves normality only under \(d_{\max}=o(n^{1/9})\), while its nonconvergence example does not identify the intervening worst-case degree frontier; generic dependency-graph bounds also discard the ordered prefix structure used by the fixed design.
project_justification.niche: The independent desired-exposure coordinates admit an exact forward Doob decomposition, and componentwise Perron priority controls both fourth moments of the increments and fluctuations of their predictable quadratic variation without imposing a maximum-outcome bound.
project_justification.fill: The proved martingale bound yields the quantitative error \(C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)\{D_n^2/(n\lambda_n)+D_n/n\}^{1/5}\), repeated stars certify failure at every fixed \(n^{2/3}\) scale, and together they establish the iff frontier \(d_n=o(n^{2/3})\). The same analysis proves spectral-bound ratio consistency and conservative feasible Wald coverage, while the graph-adaptive rule \(D_n^2/(n\lambda_n)\to0\) supplies a sufficient refinement for individual graph sequences.

body.related_work: \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} supplies the fixed \(r=2\) design, estimator, spectral variance bound, the \(o(n^{1/9})\) sufficient CLT in Theorem 5.6, the direct-effect nonconvergence construction in Proposition 5.8, additive and ratio consistency in Propositions 5.3--5.4, and the Wald result in Corollary 5.7. Its formal direct-effect conflict graph has operator \(\mathcal H_n=I_n+A_{G_n}\); Appendix D.9 writes the star value as \(\sqrt{n-1}\) by suppressing the formal loop contribution, whereas the exact loop-inclusive value is \(1+\sqrt{n-1}\). The present fixed-\(B,c\), direct-effect, component-Perron specialization strictly strengthens the published sufficient distributional and coverage regimes. \cite{HeydeBrown1970DepartureNormality} supplies the fourth-moment martingale normal-approximation theorem used in the proof; \cite{Haeusler1988MartingaleRate}, \cite{Bolthausen1982ExactMartingaleRates}, and \cite{Mourrat2013MartingaleRate} explain the role of predictable-quadratic-variation fluctuations and the unresolved exact-rate question. Theorem 2.3 of \cite{JanischLehericy2024SparseDependencyGraph}, specialized to \(\delta=4\), is the direct generic dependency-graph comparison, but it does not exploit CGD prefix products. \cite{Ross2011FundamentalsStein}, \cite{Chin2019SteinInterference}, and \cite{CaiShaoZhang2026RefinedLocalDependence} are supporting local-dependence comparisons rather than probability theorems claimed to be sharpened here. \cite{KandirosHarshawSavje2026MinimaxNetwork} optimizes designs and estimators for minimax mean-squared point-estimation risk, a different target from the fixed-CGD Kolmogorov frontier. \cite{AronowSamii2017GeneralInterference} supplies the exposure-weighted design-based baseline, and \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026OptimizedVariance} motivates estimating a conservative quadratic bound rather than the generally unidentified exact randomization variance. Declaration 18.13 of \cite{BlairCoppockHumphreys2023ResearchDesign}, modeled after \cite{GreenKrasnoCoppockFarrerLenoirZingher2016LawnSigns}, supplies the concrete \(238\)-precinct queen-adjacency direct-effect inquiry \(\operatorname{mean}(Y_{1,0}-Y_{0,0})\). The declaration itself uses Bernoulli assignment and Aronow--Samii estimation; the present theorem is an asymptotic design rule for future replications that instead adopt fixed CGD, not a retrospective validation of that analysis.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The proved \(1/5\)-power Kolmogorov bound is inherited from a general fourth-moment martingale inequality. The present argument establishes the exact convergence frontier but does not establish that this quantitative rate is constant-order sharp inside \(d=o(n^{2/3})\), nor does it optimize constants. The graph-adaptive condition \(D_n^2/(n\lambda_n)\to0\) is sufficient for an individual legal sequence and is not claimed necessary graph by graph. The variance result estimates the conservative spectral bound \(\mathrm{VB}_n\), which can strictly exceed \(\sigma_n^2\); it does not identify the exact variance.
body.honest_scope: The note fixes uniform constants \(B\) and \(c\), the finite-population direct effect, the fixed \(r=2\) CGD estimator, and componentwise Perron ordering. This is a legal fixed-design specialization using one of the anchor's permitted importance orderings, while \(\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)\) is a fixed-constant finite-\(n\) uniformization rather than literally the anchor's full asymptotic Assumptions 1--5. The fourth-moment restrictions imply the corresponding second-moment restrictions by \(n^{-1}\sum_i a_{n,i}^2\le(n^{-1}\sum_i a_{n,i}^4)^{1/2}\le\sqrt B\), and similarly for \(b_{n,i}\). Under the uniform frontier, \(\lambda_n\le D_n\le d_n=o(n^{2/3})\) implies \(\lambda_n=o(n)\); under the graph-adaptive sufficient rule, \(\lambda_n/n\le D_n^2/(n\lambda_n)\to0\). The repeated-star witnesses also satisfy \(\lambda_n=1+\sqrt{k_n}=O(n^{1/3})=o(n)\). Conversely, whenever an anchor sequence has finite uniform endpoint fourth-moment bounds and \(\liminf_n n\sigma_n^2/\lambda_n>0\), fixed constants \(B\ge1\) and \(c\in(0,1]\) can be chosen so that the sequence is eventually in \(\mathcal M_n(D_n;B,c)\). The iff claim concerns the worst-case maximum-degree envelope \(K_n(d_n;B,c)\), not necessity for each individual graph sequence. Wald coverage is conservative because \(\mathrm{VB}_n\ge\sigma_n^2\), and no exact-coverage or exact-variance-estimation claim is made. The result is an asymptotic benchmark for future fixed-CGD replications; it does not provide a finite-\(n\) certificate for the \(238\)-precinct declaration or retroactively validate its Bernoulli assignment and Aronow--Samii intervals. The only remaining mathematical gap is the exact interior Kolmogorov rate, including legal lower arrays matching its vanishing terms and optimized constants.
